revision:
1. Ground the Visual Metaphor: Replace the abstract dark void with a stylized, low-poly or silhouette mountain range in deep charcoal/smoky gradients. Position the jagged, glowing orange fire line to actively consume the mountain slope, anchoring the 'spark' (yellow circle with radial heat glow) at the origin point to visually narrate the threat to the landscape. 
2. Integrate Typography as Structure: Replace the static sans-serif headline with a tall, condensed typeface (e.g., Druk Wide) to mirror rising smoke. Align the headline 'ONE SPARK IS ENOUGH' to the right edge, stacking it so the letterforms interact with the fire line (creating a visual 'burn' or shadow effect) rather than floating in isolation. 
3. Balance Composition & Hierarchy: Place the required secondary text ('Check conditions. Extinguish completely. Protect the wild.') and 'National Forest Safety Initiative' in the bottom-right corner. This fills the previous 'dead space,' balances the visual weight of the top-left headline, and completes the diagonal reading path from spark to message. 
4. Refine Atmosphere & Craft: Apply a 'turbulence' or 'roughen' filter to the fire line to break geometric symmetry, evoking chaotic burning edges. Use a textured, smoky gradient background instead of flat blue to add atmospheric depth and emotional urgency, ensuring the high-contrast orange/blue palette remains dominant for visibility.
protected_strengths: The strong diagonal composition and high-contrast color palette (glowing orange against dark blue/charcoal) which ensure visibility and urgency.
The narrative anchor of the 'spark' at the origin point.
The bold, sans-serif typographic weight of the headline concept.
resolved_conflicts: Conflict: Abstract minimalism vs. Contextual Specificity. Resolution: Retained the minimalist diagonal structure but grounded it with a mountain silhouette to satisfy the 'landscape' requirement without cluttering the design.

Conflict: Static Text Placement vs. Dynamic Visual Energy. Resolution: Moved text from isolated corner to right-aligned stack interacting with the fire line, turning typography into an active compositional element rather than a passive label.

Conflict: Sterile Digital Aesthetic vs. Emotional Urgency. Resolution: Replaced flat colors with textured gradients and roughened vector edges to evoke heat and chaos while maintaining the clean, high-contrast visual system.
rationale: This brief prioritizes the integration of all four mandates by using the mountain silhouette to ground the abstract metaphor (Visual Concept), the right-aligned text stack to balance the diagonal composition (Composition), the condensed typeface to mirror the visual energy (Typography), and the textured gradients to enhance emotional weight (Color/Atmosphere). It avoids averaging by making specific, decisive changes that link the visual metaphor directly to the typographic hierarchy.
